A jade-scaled empress with scales carved in geometric patterns, broad ceremonial horns swept wide like cathedral arches, the largest dragon in seven territories, her brood arranged in concentric rings around her hovering, magnificent form.

A charcoal-and-amber ancient one whose every exhale scorches the air yellow, great blunt heavily scarred horns worn smooth by centuries, wings like burnt parchment, surrounded by a dense swirling cloud of smaller amber-tinged dragons.

A rose-gold twilight matriarch whose scales shift from pink to deep copper as light fades, sweeping lyrate horns adorned with old battle nicks, the evening brood trailing her in long ribboning streams across the darkening sky.

An ivory elder patriarch with scales yellowed by extreme age, massive down-curved horns draped in old shed skin, nearly twice the wingspan of any companion, the reverent brood giving him wide respectful berth as he passes.

A deep teal ocean-lord whose scales gleam like malachite below storm clouds, enormous flattened horns like whale bones, bulk so tremendous the smaller dragons struggle against the wind vortex his great wings generate in passage.

A pitch-black shadow-queen with scales that absorb all light, barely visible except for the pale gleam of her immense curving horns, the night-brood clustering tight in her absolute darkness, hidden from every watching eye below.

A flame-orange alpha male with scales that ripple like living embers, thick squared horns capped with natural carbon deposits, so much broader and longer than the surrounding dragons that he cleaves the brood formation like a prow.

A deep wine-red matriarch whose scales bear the patina of extreme old age, enormous recurved horns grown through multiple spiraling cycles, her wingspan casting shadow over thirty smaller dragons roosting reverently on the rocks beneath her.

A chalk-white albino colossus with faintly pink-tinted scales and blood-red eyes, great bladed horns stark against dark sky, so rarely seen that the surrounding dragons press close with clear displays of awed, instinctive submission.

A gunmetal-grey titan with scales interlocked like plate armor, twin parallel horns running straight and massive as siege weapons, leading a dense disciplined phalanx of smaller grey dragons across a battlefield sky thick with smoke.

A deep forest-green elder female whose scales carry decades of moss and copper-green patina, tremendous gnarled horns branching like antlers, the vast brood nesting in the canopy beneath her like birds beneath a continental storm.

A copper-scaled ancient whose surface is oxidized to vivid verdigris in patches, enormous flared horns green with age, the oldest and largest dragon in the assembled migration, hundreds of smaller copper-toned descendants streaming behind her across the sky.
A gleaming gold patriarch with swept-back gilded horns banking at the vanguard of the flight, his scales blazing like a second sun, the brood trailing in loose formation behind him.
A storm-grey sky-king crackling with arcs of lightning along his spine and horns, vast wings churning thunderheads, smaller dragons riding the turbulent winds spiraling in his wake.
A molten volcanic broodmother glowing ember-orange between her obsidian scales, venting heat haze from her nostrils, her immense bulk anchoring the roost while younger dragons circle her restlessly.
A bronze war-leader scarred from a hundred campaigns, horns blunted and scored, his broad wings casting the smaller dragons into shadow as he turns to face the approaching storm.
A regal purple monarch bearing a vivid feathered crest between his horns, scales shimmering violet and indigo, the assembled brood arrayed behind him in strict hierarchical formation.
An immense green moss-scaled elder draped in creeping lichen across her flanks and horns, ancient and slow-moving, the younger emerald and jade dragons nestled against her vast sides.
A deep sapphire ocean-lord with webbed wing-edges and salt-crusted curved horns, enormous where he crests the wave, a dozen sleeker sea-blue dragons leaping the swells around him.
A pale bone-white albino elder with translucent horn ridges and milky eyes, her sheer size silencing the brood as they part instinctively to make room for her passage.
A rust-red desert patriarch with sun-bleached horn tips and cracked scales baked to terracotta, his immense shadow sweeping the dunes as smaller ochre dragons spiral up in his thermals.
A silver-scaled storm matriarch with branching antler-like horns wreathed in frost, larger than any of her brood by half a wingspan, her breath scattering the smaller ones like leaves.
A deep charcoal-scaled mountain king with granite-grey horns wide as a fortress gate, perched immovable at the peak while his lesser kin jostle and spiral below on the updrafts.
A viridian sea-glass elder with iridescent scales and long curving jade horns, her wingspan casting the cove in green shadow, younger dragons crouching reverently on the sea-rocks around her.
A tawny amber prairie-lord with sun-yellow horns and dust-colored scales, dominating the horizon as he banks low, the scattered brood of smaller burnished dragons reforming in his slipstream.
A blood-orange titan with recurved crimson horns and scales like smoldering coal, his roar sending the smaller orange-and-black dragons scattering upward in a startled spiral around his bulk.
A chalk-white arctic elder with ice-blue horn tips and scales frosted in permanent rime, massive and slow, the pale northern brood huddled in the warmth of her folded wings.
